bug_semantics: The PATCH /api/customers/:id endpoint is reachable without an authenticated admin or customer session and trusts the attacker-controlled path UUID as the record to update. Its only route-local middleware parses JSON; the handler selects that UUID, spreads attacker-controlled fields (including email and password) into the customer update, and returns the updated record without checking that the caller owns the customer, enabling unauthenticated account takeover and lockout.
flaw_origin: Commit a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095 first made the predeclared /customers/:id route operational by adding updateCustomer.js and body-parser middleware while simultaneously adding the global API auth middleware whose explicit rule treated every route with no access property as public. The route then had no access property, so the new mutating handler was unauthenticated from its first executable revision. Commit 4b97829de4acc674cd2282af3d2b61ec3416f72b later changed the default to private but explicitly labeled this route public, preserving rather than originating the flaw.
ai_marker: absent: the raw commit object for a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095 names author and committer The Nguyen <6950941+treoden@users.noreply.github.com>, has the single message 'RESTful api implementation', has no trailers (including Co-Authored-By or Generated-with), and neither commit-object identity is a bot.
evidence: First-party report https://github.com/evershopcommerce/evershop/issues/952 documents unauthenticated PATCH /api/customers/:id account takeover, identifies route.json, the body-parser-only middleware, and updateCustomer.js, and records the maintainer's statement that it was fixed in v2.2.1. The GitHub advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-m3qj-pp48-6w2p describes the same mechanism and states that v2.2.1 changes access to private.

git diff 4e518e617b76928656936e0048da852229acf24e a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095 -- packages/evershop/src/modules/customer/api/updateCustomer shows a2f514... adding [context]bodyParser[auth].js, payloadSchema.json, and updateCustomer.js. The new handler selects and updates customer where uuid equals request.params.id, spreads request.body into the update, and performs no authentication or ownership check.

The same a2f514... diff adds packages/evershop/src/modules/auth/api/global/[jwtTokenVerify]auth.js with the comment 'Missing access property means public' and the condition !currentRoute?.access || currentRoute?.access === 'public', which calls next(). At that revision route.json contains only PATCH and /customers/:id, so the newly operational mutation endpoint bypasses auth.

Immediate-parent tree verification against 4e518e617b76928656936e0048da852229acf24e: git ls-tree shows only updateCustomer/route.json; git cat-file -e for updateCustomer/updateCustomer.js and auth/api/global/[jwtTokenVerify]auth.js both fail because neither path exists. The parent route has no access property. Thus the executable unauthenticated update mechanism is absent from the immediate parent.

git log -S"where('uuid', '=', request.params.id)" -- updateCustomer.js resolves the vulnerable UUID-based update code to a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095. git log -S'"access": "public"' -- route.json resolves the later explicit public label to 4b97829de4acc674cd2282af3d2b61ec3416f72b and its removal to f92b832255102af8db796245db01e38ea70504e9. git log -L on the route confirms that sequence.

git show 4b97829de4acc674cd2282af3d2b61ec3416f72b shows a coordinated access-model change: the global auth rule changes from missing-is-public to only explicit-public, while updateCustomer/route.json gains access public. Because the endpoint was already public by omission, this commit preserves the vulnerable behavior and is not the smallest BIC.

At tag v2.1.2, route.json still says access public; [getCurrentUser]auth.ts calls next() for public routes; the only route-local middleware parses JSON; and updateCustomer.js hashes an attacker-supplied password, updates the UUID from request.params.id, and returns the updated customer. This directly matches the published attack path.

Fix commit f92b832255102af8db796245db01e38ea70504e9 changes only updateCustomer/route.json from access public to access private. Its parent 8861498694b46f944767c49cc03180a96b38aac3 contains public, while tag v2.2.1 contains private.

Version ancestry checks: a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095 is an ancestor of the repository's earliest available release tag 1.0.0-rc.9 and all later tags through v2.1.2; f92b832255102af8db796245db01e38ea70504e9 is not an ancestor of v2.1.2 and is an ancestor of v2.2.1. git tag --contains f92b832... returns only v2.2.1, establishing the observed vulnerable/patched boundary despite the advisory listing package ranges as unknown.

git cat-file -p a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095 shows one parent, human author/committer The Nguyen, the plain subject 'RESTful api implementation', and no commit-message trailers or AI/bot marker. No squash/member history is exposed by the commit object; it is treated as the smallest available public-history commit, not decomposed.
reasoning: The advisory's explicit public line is not by itself the first causal point. The route JSON was created earlier in 4e518e6..., but that parent had no update handler and therefore lacked the dangerous mutation. Commit a2f514... added both the unauthenticated-by-default global auth behavior and the UUID-directed customer update handler, creating the complete exploit path in one smallest reachable commit. Its parent directly lacks both new code paths. The later 4b9782... access refactor merely translated the already-public omission into an explicit public declaration, so selecting it would mistake a preservation refactor for the BIC. Subsequent refactors, database migration, password hashing, and formatting retained the same missing-authorization mechanism through v2.1.2. The one-line direct fix f92b832... makes the route private and is included in v2.2.1 but not v2.1.2. Finally, BIC-only commit-object inspection provides no AI authorship or co-authorship signal, so the supported closed verdict is NOT_AI.
